target_persona: Brand, Product, Docs, Growth or Operations

evidence.fact: Ghost describes itself as a non-profit organisation building open-source technology for modern publishing and publicly lists a cross-functional team including engineering/development, product, design, brand, support and infrastructure roles.
Ghost's official docs repository uses a GitHub pull-request workflow; the Mintlify GitHub App creates PR previews and merging to main triggers deployment to docs.ghost.org.
Ghost documents a monorepo testing workflow where contributors run pnpm check and relevant test suites before opening a pull request.
Ghost markets the product to businesses as a measurable content-marketing platform and supports custom website design and themes.
Ghost publicly reports a sustainable paid hosted business around its open-source core and publishes operating metrics on its About page.

hypotheses.statement: A plausible Sparkles wedge is helping brand, product, docs or operations teammates make bounded website, documentation or product-surface changes while retaining Ghost's existing PR preview, testing and merge controls.
The strongest proof is likely reduced engineering interruption and faster cross-functional iteration, not novelty around AI itself.

unknowns: Whether Ghost has a meaningful queue of non-engineering requests waiting on engineering.
Whether non-engineering teammates already use coding agents directly against production repositories.
Who would own the workflow and budget.
Current employee count and engineering-team size were intentionally left unset rather than inferred from public team listings.
